title: "There could always be room for improvement": Posey County residents raise concerns over road safety - NewsBreak
text:
By Ian Young Isaiah Calalang ,
1 hours ago
POSEY COUNTY, Ind. (WEHT) — The Evansville Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) is working to put together a safety action plan to help improve the roads in Posey County.
Some residents are hopeful for these changes but remain cautious.
“Steps to improve, any sort of driving will naturally be incredibly helpful, incredibly useful,” says resident Joseph Phillips. “I just wish that it’s done consistently.”
MPO is collaborating with Posey County leaders to help make its roads safer. MPO officials say they surveyed the roads themselves but add the public’s thoughts and ideas are necessary to move forward.
“The data tells us one thing, but if we can get information from the public that we might not be seeing through the data, that would definitely be helpful for the plan,” says Matt Schriefer with MPO.
“We’d like to study where and why accidents are happening and take steps to see if we can reduce that over the next ten years,” says Phillips.
More than 200 people have already weighed in pointing to problem areas across the county. One of the top concerns was visibility at stop signs. Phillips says he’s a new driver who found that to be an issue after a close call on the road.
“There was such a large bush on the way, I couldn’t see a guy mowing his grass,” says Phillips. “So, we had to quickly skirt out of the way. Stuff around the streets themselves aren’t being maintained to where you can’t see what’s on the sidewalk, even the safest driver is going to get into an accident if they can’t see what’s around them.”
Residents like Fletcher Wheeler believe problems always arise on the roads but is hopeful to see what the county does to help improve it.
“I know not everything is going to be perfect,” says Wheeler. “Nothing is really perfect, but there could always be room for improvement whether it be fixing the visibility for signs or potholes on the road. I think that’s great that they’re trying to do all that.”
MPO officials say they’ll use that feedback to build a safety plan with a goal of having it ready by the end of summer.
